questions.question: In traversing non-empty binary tree, visit the root is made in the last in -
questions.explanation: In Postorder traversal, the root is visited LAST — order is Left → Right → Root.

questions.question: The in-order and post-order traversal of a binary tree are DBEAFC and DEBFCA respectively. What will be the total number of nodes in the left sub tree of the given tree?
questions.explanation: Root is A (last in postorder). Inorder: DBE|A|FC — left subtree has nodes D, B, E = 3 nodes.

questions.question: A B-tree is -
questions.explanation: A B-tree is always balanced (all leaves at same level) and ordered (keys maintain sorted order).

questions.question: A Binary tree is a type of tree -

options.B: such that no node has degree more than 2
options.C: For which both (a) and (b) above are correct
options.D: in which non-leaf nodes will have degree 2

questions.explanation: A binary tree is both ordered (left/right distinction matters) and restricts each node to at most degree 2.

questions.question: In array representation of Binary tree, if the index number of a child node is 6 then the index number of its parent node is -
questions.explanation: Parent index = floor(child index / 2) = floor(6/2) = 3.

questions.question: How many different order traversals are applicable to a binary tree (In General)?
questions.explanation: Three standard traversals apply to a binary tree: Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of children that a binary tree node can have?
questions.explanation: By definition, a binary tree node can have at most 2 children — left child and right child.

questions.question: In a full binary tree if the number of internal nodes is I, then the number of leaves L are -
questions.explanation: In a full binary tree, the number of leaf nodes = number of internal nodes + 1, i.e., L = I + 1.

questions.question: The depth of root node is -
questions.explanation: The root node is at depth 0 — depth is the number of edges from root to the node.

questions.question: A binary tree of height h has at least h nodes and at most -
questions.explanation: A binary tree of height h can have at most 2^(h+1) - 1 nodes (complete binary tree). Option D represents 2^h - 1 which applies to height h-1 interpretation — maximum is 2^(h+1)-1.

questions.question: When the left sub-tree of the tree is one level higher than that of the right sub-tree, then the balance factor is -
questions.explanation: Balance factor = height(left subtree) - height(right subtree). Left is higher by 1, so BF = +1.

questions.question: Total number of nodes at the nth level of a binary tree can be given as -
questions.explanation: At level n of a binary tree, the maximum number of nodes is 2^n (root is at level 0).

questions.question: A graph in which there exists a path between two of its nodes is called -
questions.explanation: A connected graph is one where there exists a path between every pair of vertices.

questions.question: The total number of edges containing the node u is called -
questions.explanation: The degree of a node is the total number of edges incident to (containing) that node.

questions.question: The data structure required for Breadth First Search on a graph is -
questions.explanation: BFS uses a queue to explore nodes level by level — enqueue neighbours and dequeue to visit.

questions.question: For an undirected graph with n vertices and e edges, the sum of the degree of each vertex is equal to -
questions.explanation: In an undirected graph, each edge contributes 2 to the total degree sum, so sum of degrees = 2e.

questions.question: The memory use of an adjacency matrix is:
questions.explanation: An adjacency matrix requires an n×n array to represent a graph with n vertices, so memory = O(n²).

questions.question: Preorder is nothing but -
questions.explanation: Preorder traversal (Root → Left → Right) follows the same principle as Depth First Search on a tree.

questions.question: Binary trees with threads are called as -
questions.explanation: Binary trees where NULL pointers are replaced by threads (pointers to inorder successor/predecessor) are called Threaded trees.

questions.question: In Binary trees nodes with no successor are called -
questions.explanation: Nodes with no children (no successors) in a binary tree are called terminal nodes or leaf nodes.

questions.question: The depth Dn of a complete binary tree of n nodes given by -
questions.explanation: The depth of a complete binary tree with n nodes is Dn = floor(log₂(n+1)) or log₂(n+1) rounded down.

questions.question: Every node N in a binary tree T except the root has a unique parent called the ________ of N.
questions.explanation: The unique node directly above N is called the Parent of N — not predecessor, antecedent, or precursor.

questions.question: The in-order traversal of tree will yield a sorted listing of elements of tree in ________.
questions.explanation: Inorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree (BST) yields elements in sorted ascending order.

questions.question: The post-order traversal of a binary tree is DEBFCA. Find out the pre-order traversal -
questions.explanation: Root is A (last in postorder). Reconstruct tree: preorder gives Root→Left→Right = ABDECF.

questions.question: Three standards ways of traversing a binary tree T with root R -
questions.explanation: The three standard binary tree traversals are Pre-order (Root-Left-Right), In-order (Left-Root-Right), and Post-order (Left-Right-Root).

questions.question: A full binary tree with n leaves contains -
questions.explanation: A full binary tree with n leaf nodes has exactly 2n - 1 total nodes (n leaves + n-1 internal nodes).

questions.question: Which of the following data structure is nonlinear type?
questions.explanation: Graph is a nonlinear data structure — elements have complex relationships, not a simple sequence.

questions.question: Which of the following is non-linear data structure?
questions.explanation: Trees are non-linear data structures — nodes are arranged in hierarchical levels, not a sequence.

questions.question: What is a leaf node?
questions.explanation: A leaf node (terminal node) is a node that has no children in the tree.

questions.question: Degree of a leaf node of a binary tree is -
questions.explanation: A leaf node has no children, so its degree (number of children) is 0.

questions.question: The height of a binary tree is the maximum number of edges in any root to leaf path. The maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h is -
questions.explanation: Maximum nodes in binary tree of height h = 2^(h+1) - 1, achieved when every level is completely filled.

questions.question: How are graphs represented inside a computer's memory? Which method do you prefer and why?
questions.explanation: Graphs can be represented using adjacency matrix (O(n²) space) or adjacency list (O(n+e) space) — choice depends on density.
